facts.text: On this date in 1904, the New York City subway opened — the first line ran from City Hall to 145th Street and carried 150,000 riders in a single day, more than any city planner had dared predict.

On this date in 1962, the Cuban Missile Crisis reached its peak: a Soviet submarine nearly launched a nuclear torpedo after losing contact with Moscow, stopped only because one officer, Vasili Arkhipov, refused to authorize it.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Chengdu, China than live outside it — roughly half of all humanity fits within that single radius.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, with over 71,000 people per square kilometer — nearly twice the density of Dhaka, its closest rival.
Indonesia spans more time zones than the continental United States and contains over 17,000 islands, yet more than half its 280 million people live on a single one: Java.
On this day in 1929, the Dow fell 13% — Black Tuesday. The crash wiped out $14 billion in a single session, equal to roughly $250 billion today.
On Oct 27, 1997, the NYSE invoked circuit breakers for the first time ever, halting trading after the Dow dropped 554 points during the Asian financial crisis.
The Amsterdam Stock Exchange, founded in 1602, didn't just invent the stock market — it invented short selling, options, and margin trading simultaneously.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2.4 trillion valuation in 2022, making it worth more than the entire GDP of France.
The S&P 500 has historically risen in the six months following a U.S. midterm election every single time since 1950 — a streak across 19 consecutive cycles.

On this date in 1905, Einstein submitted his paper on special relativity. Time dilation it describes isn't theoretical — GPS satellites must correct for it daily or navigation errors would compound by 11 km per day.
On this date in 1961, NASA launched the Saturn SA-1. Its first stage burned 15 tons of fuel per second — enough to drain an Olympic pool in under 3 minutes.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces the lining of your small intestine every 2 to 4 days. The cells doing the most digestive work are among the shortest-lived in the human body.
Sound cannot travel through space, but pressure waves can move through stars. Astronomers detect these stellar oscillations to map what lies thousands of kilometers beneath a star's surface.
On this day in 1682, Philadelphia was founded — making the city older than the piano, the steam engine, and the United States itself.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates the civilization Cortés destroyed.
On this day in 1904, the New York City subway opened. The entire system was built faster than a single modern subway station gets approved today.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was ancient history to ancient Egyptians.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before the telephone. Alexander Bain could send a document across a wire before anyone could make a call.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast it now appears in several translation dictionaries.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. The word fuses homesickness, grief, and nostalgia into a single ache that English has never managed to name.
On this day in 1682, William Penn landed in Pennsylvania — a colony whose name he tried to refuse, finding it embarrassingly self-promotional. The king insisted.
On this day in 1904, the New York City subway opened. The word 'subway' itself is a compression of 'subterranean way,' first used in print in 1825 for an underground aqueduct.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word meaning a look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. It holds a Guinness record as the most succinct word in any language.
On this date in 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper to a cryptography mailing list. Nine people were on the thread. None of them believed it would work.
On this date in 2021, Ethereum completed its transition to a proof-of-stake testnet merge on Goerli — the dry run before the real Merge that would cut ETH issuance by ~90%.
Bitcoin's genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as poetry, but as a timestamp. It proves no bitcoin was pre-mined before Jan 3, 2009.

The largest single Bitcoin transaction ever recorded moved 500,000 BTC in November 2011. It was a wallet consolidation by Mt. Gox. The coins were never fully accounted for after the exchange collapsed.
Ethereum smart contracts have no native way to trigger themselves. Every on-chain action requires an external account to pay gas and send a transaction — there is no autonomous execution.
Today in 1955, Bobby Fischer was born — the same year John McCarthy coined the term 'artificial intelligence' at Dartmouth. Both were prodigies; only one was eventually beaten by a machine.
Today in 2016, Google announced it had deployed WaveNet in production — a neural text-to-speech system that cut the gap between machine and human speech quality in half, overnight.
GPT-4 was trained on roughly 25,000 NVIDIA A100s running for months. The electricity cost alone exceeded what most countries spend annually on their entire national research budgets.
AlphaFold2 predicted the 3D structure of virtually every known protein — around 200 million — in under a year. Structural biologists had spent 50 years solving roughly 170,000 by hand.
The first neural network to beat humans at Go, AlphaGo, was itself beaten 100–0 by its successor AlphaGo Zero, which learned the game from scratch with no human game data in three days.
